questions.question_text: In the 'stages of change' proposed by Prochaska and DiClemente:

options.text: The contemplation stage occurs after the decision stage
The last stage is the maintenance stage
The stage at which the user attempts the change is called the action stage
The action stage occurs before the contemplation stage
The precontemplation stage is when the user accepts that there is a problem and looks at the positive and negative aspects of drug use

correct_answer.text: The stage at which the user attempts the change is called the action stage

correct_answers.text: The stage at which the user attempts the change is called the action stage

questions.explanation: The stages described by Prochaska and DiClemente are precontemplation, contemplation, decision, action, maintenance and relapse, respectively. Precontemplation is the first of the stages, when a user continues using his or her drug and does not perceive it as a problem. The second stage is contemplation, when a user accepts that there may be a problem. The action stage is when a user attempts to change his or her behaviour. The maintenance stage is when a user continues the abstinence and tries to improve. Relapse is when a user goes back to his or her drug use behaviour.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a feature of substance dependence as described by Edwards and Gross?

options.text: Primacy of drug-seeking behaviour
Widening of drug-taking repertoire
Signs of withdrawal on attempted abstinence
Increased tolerance to the effects of the drug
Rapid reinstatement of previous pattern of drug use after abstinence

correct_answer.text: Widening of drug-taking repertoire

correct_answers.text: Widening of drug-taking repertoire

questions.explanation: A narrowing of repertoire is seen in drug dependence, when a user moves from a range of drugs to a single drug taken in preference to all others.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not equivalent to one unit of alcohol?

options.text: Half a pint of 4% beer
One small measure of whiskey
One standard glass of 12% wine
One bottle (330 ml) of 4% lager
One small glass of 10% sparkling wine

correct_answer.text: One standard glass of 12% wine

correct_answers.text: One standard glass of 12% wine

questions.explanation: One standard glass is 175 ml. Hence 12% wine in a standard glass is equivalent to 2.1 units. A pint is 568 ml. One small glass is 125 ml. An easy way to find the number of units is to multiply strength by the volume or measure in ml and divide by 1000.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false?

options.text: The NHS recommends women should not drink more than 2–3 units of alcohol per day on a regular basis
In the UK, roughly 93% of men and 87% of women drink alcohol
In the UK, the legal age for buying alcohol is 18 years
The NHS recommends men should not drink more than 3–4 units of alcohol per day on a regular basis
The lower limit for women is because they have a higher ratio of water to fat than men

correct_answer.text: The lower limit for women is because they have a higher ratio of water to fat than men

correct_answers.text: The lower limit for women is because they have a higher ratio of water to fat than men

questions.explanation: Daily limit has been given more importance. It is recommended that men should have no more than 3–4 units per day and women should have no more than 2–3 units per day. The lower limits for women are due to women's higher ratio of fat to water and hence inability to dilute the alcohol consumed.

questions.question_text: Regarding the CAGE questionnaire, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: All of the above
It is a screening questionnaire
It asks whether a person feels like cutting back on his or her drinking
There is a question on whether a person feels guilty about his or her drinking
It asks about having a drink early in the morning as an 'eye-opener'

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: The CAGE questionnaire is used for screening and consists of questions on Cutting down on drinking, getting Annoyed by people criticizing drinking pattern, feeling Guilty, and using alcohol as an Eye-opener.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding tests used in alcohol dependence?

options.text: The MCV level remains raised for 3–6 months after increased alcohol consumption
A raised gGT level is pathognomic of heavy drinking
Carbohydrate-deficient transferrin level in blood shows around 70% sensitivity
A breath test is useful in assessing recent consumption
The CAGE questionnaire is used for screening

correct_answer.text: A raised gGT level is pathognomic of heavy drinking

correct_answers.text: A raised gGT level is pathognomic of heavy drinking

questions.explanation: The gGT level can be raised in other liver diseases, especially chronic diseases. Blood tests are not specific/sensitive enough for routine screening purposes.

questions.question_text: Regarding harm reduction, which of the following statements is false?

options.text: Motivation is a prerequisite for drug abstinence
Stages of change were described by Prochaska and DiClemente
The maintenance stage is followed by relapse
The contemplation stage is when a user attempts change
The maintenance stage comes after the decision stage

correct_answer.text: The contemplation stage is when a user attempts change

correct_answers.text: The contemplation stage is when a user attempts change

questions.explanation: The stages described by Prochaska and DiClemente are precontemplation, contemplation, decision, action, maintenance and relapse. The contemplation stage is when the user accepts that he or she may have a problem. The user attempts to change at the action stage.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding delirium tremens, except:

options.text: There is a reported mortality of 5–10%
It may present with tactile or visual hallucinations
It always occurs in clear consciousness
It can occur even 5 days after the last drink
It is a medical emergency that requires inpatient medical care

correct_answer.text: It always occurs in clear consciousness

correct_answers.text: It always occurs in clear consciousness

questions.explanation: Delirium tremens is a medical emergency whereby a person goes into an acute confusional state secondary to alcohol withdrawal. It usually occurs within the first 2 days but can present as many as 7 days after the last drink. Features include clouding of consciousness, disorientation, amnesia for recent events, marked psychomotor agitation and hallucinations.

questions.question_text: Regarding maintenance therapy, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Disulfiram is usually prescribed once abstinence is achieved
Acamprosate produces an aversive action if taken with alcohol
Naltrexone acts as an anti-craving agent
Naltrexone acts by antagonizing the effects of endogenous endorphins released by alcohol consumption
Disulfiram acts by inhibiting acetaldehyde dehydrogenase

correct_answer.text: Acamprosate produces an aversive action if taken with alcohol

correct_answers.text: Acamprosate produces an aversive action if taken with alcohol

questions.explanation: Disulfiram acts as an aversive drug by irreversibly inhibiting acetaldehyde dehydrogenase. Acamprosate and naltrexone act as anti-craving agents. Unlike disulfiram, they do not produce aversive effects if alcohol is consumed with them.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true of Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome?

options.text: The pathology is due to neuronal degeneration following vitamin B6 deficiency
It is characterized by a wide-based gait
Ophthalmoplegia is due to optic nerve damage
With treatment, confusion and ophthalmoplegia are first to resolve
People with the syndrome usually have clear consciousness

correct_answer.text: With treatment, confusion and ophthalmoplegia are first to resolve

correct_answers.text: With treatment, confusion and ophthalmoplegia are first to resolve

questions.explanation: Wernicke's encephalopathy is characterized by a classic tetrad of symptoms: acute confusional state, ophthalmoplegia, nystagmus and ataxia. It is due to neuronal degeneration following thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency. Confusion and ophthalmoplegia are first to resolve.

questions.question_text: Regarding Korsakoff's psychosis, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: There is significant impairment in the ability to lay down new memories
Working memory is unimpaired
Procedural memory is grossly impaired
It is most commonly caused by thiamine deficiency
The presumed mechanism involves a lesion in the mammillothalamic pathway

correct_answer.text: Procedural memory is grossly impaired

correct_answers.text: Procedural memory is grossly impaired

questions.explanation: Retrograde amnesia as well as difficulty in laying down new memories is seen. However, procedural memory, emotional memory and working memory are unimpaired. It is presumed that thiamine deficiency causes lesions in the mammillothalamic tract.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a medical complication of alcohol misuse?

options.text: Fatty change in liver
Peptic ulceration
Gout
Tuberculosis
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Most of the systems are affected by alcohol misuse. It also causes erectile dysfunction, foetal alcohol syndrome and osteoporosis.

questions.question_text: In the UK, what is the percentage of adults who have tried illegal drugs in their lifetime?
questions.explanation: About one-third of the adult population in the UK have tried illegal drugs at least once in their lifetime.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is untrue?

options.text: MDMA is an abbreviation for methyldioxy-N-methamphetamine
MDMA causes serotonin release and blocks uptake
The 'rush' following MDMA intake lasts for around 3 hours
Death can occur after MDMA use, through dehydration and hyperthermia
MDMA has hallucinogenic and stimulant properties

correct_answer.text: MDMA is an abbreviation for methyldioxy-N-methamphetamine

correct_answers.text: MDMA is an abbreviation for methyldioxy-N-methamphetamine

questions.explanation: MDMA is 3,4,methylenedioxy-N-methamphetamine. It causes serotonin release and blocks uptake. It has hallucinogenic and stimulant properties by potentiating neurotransmission and increasing cortical excitability.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding cocaine intake?

options.text: The main route of intake is by injection
Cocaine acts as a cortical depressant
The effect of the drug lasts for a long time because it is metabolized slowly
Cocaine addiction is treated by substitute prescribing
Acute harmful effects include arrhythmia, intense anxiety and hypertension

correct_answer.text: Acute harmful effects include arrhythmia, intense anxiety and hypertension

correct_answers.text: Acute harmful effects include arrhythmia, intense anxiety and hypertension

questions.explanation: Cocaine is a stimulant and has a euphoric action that lasts only for short periods as it is metabolized fast in the body. The main route of intake is by inhalation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding benzodiazepines?

options.text: They cause dependency
They are usually taken orally
Temazepam is a short-acting benzodiazepine
They do not cause cross-tolerance with other drugs in the group
They enhance GABA transmission

correct_answer.text: They do not cause cross-tolerance with other drugs in the group

correct_answers.text: They do not cause cross-tolerance with other drugs in the group

questions.explanation: Benzodiazepines produce tolerance rapidly with themselves as well as with others in the benzodiazepine group. Their mode of action is by enhancing GABA transmission.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding LSD, except:

options.text: It is a hallucinogen
LSD is an abbreviation for lysergic acid diethylamide
Its use can lead to 'bad trips'
Chronic use leads to flashbacks
Physiological dependence and withdrawal symptoms are very common

correct_answer.text: Physiological dependence and withdrawal symptoms are very common

correct_answers.text: Physiological dependence and withdrawal symptoms are very common

questions.explanation: LSD is a hallucinogen. Its effect lasts for 6 hours after ingestion. It does not cause physiological dependence or withdrawal symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an immediate effect of cannabis intake?

options.text: Depression
Agitation
Low appetite
Bradycardia
Ataxia

correct_answer.text: Ataxia

correct_answers.text: Ataxia

questions.explanation: Cannabis is the most commonly used illegal drug. The immediate effects include euphoria, enhanced sense of well-being, relaxation, increased appetite, mild tachycardia, variable dysarthria and ataxia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following medications has been prescribed for opiate withdrawal?

options.text: Lofexidine
Loperamide
Metoclopramide
Ibuprofen
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Lofexidine is used for hypertension and ibuprofen for headaches and muscle pain.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding opiate maintenance therapy?

options.text: It should be reviewed daily over the first week of starting therapy
Dose should be increased by 5–10 mg in the first days if needed
Stabilization may take up to 6 weeks
Rapid reduction is achieved within a week
Slow reduction is over a 4- to 6-month period

correct_answer.text: Rapid reduction is achieved within a week

correct_answers.text: Rapid reduction is achieved within a week

questions.explanation: Rapid reduction is achieved in 14–21 days.

questions.question_text: Regarding driving and drug misuse, which of the following statements is false?

options.text: A conviction for alcohol misuse may incur loss of licence for up to 6 months
Alcohol dependence incurs loss of licence for 1 year
Dependency on cannabis and LSD may incur loss of licence for 6 months
Dependency on heroin or cocaine may incur loss of licence for 3 months
Medical screening and a urine test may be required when reinstating a licence

correct_answer.text: Dependency on heroin or cocaine may incur loss of licence for 3 months

correct_answers.text: Dependency on heroin or cocaine may incur loss of licence for 3 months

questions.explanation: Dependency on heroin or cocaine may incur loss of licence for 1 year.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an internal trigger to drink?

options.text: Anxiety
View of a pub
Smell of alcohol
Pressure of work
Seeing one's friends drinking

correct_answer.text: Anxiety

correct_answers.text: Anxiety

questions.explanation: Anxiety is an internal trigger to drink.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding motivational interviewing for alcohol addiction?

options.text: The therapist needs to be highly motivated
The patient is encouraged to come up with solutions for his or her drinking problem
The therapist gives a choice of solutions to the patient
The therapist strongly persuades the patient to stop drinking
The patient has only a passive role in the therapy

correct_answer.text: The patient is encouraged to come up with solutions for his or her drinking problem

correct_answers.text: The patient is encouraged to come up with solutions for his or her drinking problem

questions.explanation: In motivational interviewing, the patient plays the active role and is encouraged to find solutions for his or her drinking problem.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: The setting in which opiate detoxification is carried out affects the outcome
There is no evidence base for motivational interviewing in the treatment of drug misuse
Advice on safer injecting practices includes using the same injection site
A hand signature is always required in controlled drug prescription
A shorter-acting opiate is preferred for substitute prescribing

correct_answer.text: A hand signature is always required in controlled drug prescription

correct_answers.text: A hand signature is always required in controlled drug prescription

questions.explanation: Research has shown that the setting of opiate detoxification does not affect the outcome. Advice is given to rotate injection sites. Longer-acting opiates like methadone are used in substitute prescribing.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding cigarette smoking?

options.text: No difference in prevalence of smoking has been noted between psychosis and neurosis
Smoking is less common in lower socioeconomic classes
80% of smokers start before the age of 19
Women are more likely than men to smoke cigarettes
Most smokers quit after doctor's advice

correct_answer.text: 80% of smokers start before the age of 19

correct_answers.text: 80% of smokers start before the age of 19

questions.explanation: Approximately 80% of smokers start smoking before the age of 19 (based on data from the 2006 SAMHSA National Household Survey on Drug Use and Health, available at: www.oas.samhsa.gov/nsduh.htm). Men are more likely to smoke than women. 2% stop smoking within a year after advice from clinicians.

questions.question_text: All of the following can be classed as negligent prescriptions, except:

options.text: Failure to treat adverse effects that have or should have been recognized
Unreasonable mixing of drugs
Patient having side-effects from medications prescribed
Prescribing too many drugs at one time
Failing to disclose side-effects of medication

correct_answer.text: Patient having side-effects from medications prescribed

correct_answers.text: Patient having side-effects from medications prescribed

questions.explanation: The patient needs to be well informed of the side-effects of the medication prescribed, as well as of with the effects. As long as the patient is well informed of the effects and side-effects and monitored for them, a prescription would not be deemed negligent. However, other practices like unreasonable mixing of drugs, or prescribing too many drugs, could be classed as negligent prescription.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an indication for seclusion?

options.text: Extremely unstable medical and psychiatric conditions
Overtly suicidal patient
Delirious or demented patient unable to tolerate decreased stimulation
For punishment of the patient, or the convenience of staff
To assist in treatment as part of ongoing behaviour therapy

correct_answer.text: To assist in treatment as part of ongoing behaviour therapy

correct_answers.text: To assist in treatment as part of ongoing behaviour therapy

questions.explanation: Seclusion and restraint raise many legal issues and indications need to be documented and discussed. Indications include preventing imminent harm to patient or others, preventing significant disruption to a treatment programme, and decreasing sensory overstimulation.

questions.question_text: For a person to have capacity, all of the following are necessary, except:

options.text: The person should be able to understand the information
The person should be able to believe the information
The person should be able to weigh up the risks and benefits
The person should be able to retain the information for an adequate time
The person should be able to communicate his or her decision

correct_answer.text: The person should be able to believe the information

correct_answers.text: The person should be able to believe the information

questions.explanation: To have capacity, a person needs to understand, weigh the risks and benefits, retain the information and communicate his or her decision.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding a person's fitness to plead?

options.text: He or she should be able to comprehend the course of proceedings of the trial, so as to make a proper defence
He or she should know that any jurors to whom he or she may have an objection may be challenged
He or she should be able to comprehend the evidence
He or she should be able to give proper instructions to his or her legal representatives
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: A person should fulfil Pritchard's criteria to be fit to plead.

questions.question_text: What percentage of people guilty of indecent exposure are first-time offenders?
questions.explanation: 20% of first-time offenders go on to commit further indecent exposure. 60% of those with previous sexual offences and 70% with previous sexual and non-sexual offences commit further indecent exposure.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding sexual offences?

options.text: Indecent exposure is the most common sexual offence
Female children are victimized more than males
50% of rapists reoffend sexually
Intrafamilial abuse is usually by father to daughter or step-father to step-daughter
Extrafamilial abuse is less common than intrafamilial

correct_answer.text: 50% of rapists reoffend sexually

correct_answers.text: 50% of rapists reoffend sexually

questions.explanation: The rate of reoffending among sex offenders is low. Only 15% of rapists reoffend sexually and 20% commit violent non-sexual offences.

questions.question_text: What percentage of violent crime in Britain is by people with schizophrenia?

options.text: More than 50%
More than 70%
Less than 30%
Less than 50%
Less than 10%

correct_answer.text: Less than 10%

correct_answers.text: Less than 10%

questions.explanation: People with schizophrenia account for less than 10% of all violent crimes in Britain.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false?

options.text: People with milder forms of learning disability are more likely to offend than those with severe learning disability
Epilepsy is twice as common in offenders as in the general population
Alcohol- and drug-related problems are strongly linked to violence
Depression is commonly associated with violence or aggression
Personality disorder is more strongly related to offending and violence than mental illness

correct_answer.text: Depression is commonly associated with violence or aggression

correct_answers.text: Depression is commonly associated with violence or aggression

questions.explanation: Depression is very rarely associated with violence or offending. Affective disorders are less commonly associated with offending and violence than schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an actuarial risk assessment tool?

options.text: VRAG (Violence Risk Appraisal Guide)
HCR-20 (Historical Clinical Risk Management 20)
PCL-R (Psychopathy Checklist–Revised)
ROR (Risk of Reconviction score)
RPS (Reconviction Prediction Score)

correct_answer.text: HCR-20 (Historical Clinical Risk Management 20)

correct_answers.text: HCR-20 (Historical Clinical Risk Management 20)

questions.explanation: Risk assessment tools can be either structured clinical or actuarial. The HCR-20 is a structured clinical tool, while all the others are actuarial tools.

questions.question_text: What percentage of people held in police custody suffer from mental disorder?
questions.explanation: 2–5% of people held in police custody suffer from mental disorder.

questions.question_text: A patient discharged from hospital has been violent and aggressive at home after being non-compliant with his medications. The approved mental health practitioner who went out to see him has not been able to get access to the house. The use of which section of the Mental Health Act would be most appropriate in these conditions?

options.text: Section 4
Section 135
Section 2
Section 5(2)
Section 136

correct_answer.text: Section 135

correct_answers.text: Section 135

questions.explanation: The approved mental health practitioner should apply for a section 135 for the police to break into the patient's house and bring him to the hospital or nearest place of safety.

questions.question_text: Regarding crime, which of the following statements is false?

options.text: Males between the age of 10 and 20 years account for 50% of crime
Females account for only 20% of offenders
Robbery is one of the most common crimes
Low intelligence is associated with offending
The peak age for committing crime among females is 12–15 years

correct_answer.text: Robbery is one of the most common crimes

correct_answers.text: Robbery is one of the most common crimes

questions.explanation: Robbery is one of the rarest forms of crime. The most common ones are theft, burglary, criminal damage and car crime.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Victims of homicide are usually males
Perpetrators of crime are usually females
The majority of homicide offenders are mentally disordered
5% of victims of homicide are known to offenders
50% of homicide cases result in a finding of diminished responsibility

correct_answer.text: Victims of homicide are usually males

correct_answers.text: Victims of homicide are usually males

questions.explanation: About 70% of homicide victims are males. Males (80–90%) are the main perpetrators of crime.

questions.question_text: What percentage of incidents of arson are successfully prosecuted?
questions.explanation: Less than 20% of cases of arson lead to prosecution.

questions.question_text: The lifetime risk of violence in people with schizophrenia compared with that in the general population is:

options.text: Equal
50 times higher
10 times higher
30 times higher
5 times higher

correct_answer.text: 5 times higher

correct_answers.text: 5 times higher

questions.explanation: The lifetime risk of violence in people with schizophrenia is five times greater than in the general population.

questions.question_text: What percentage of prisoners are transferred to psychiatric hospitals?
questions.explanation: About 2–5% of prisoners are transferred to psychiatric hospitals.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding the MHA 2007?

options.text: Section 48 allows transfer of mentally disordered sentenced prisoners to hospital
Section 47 need reports from two registered medical practitioners
Section 41 is a restriction order
Section 49 allows the Secretary of State to add a 'restriction direction' to a transfer direction
Section 41 is issued by the Crown Court

correct_answer.text: Section 48 allows transfer of mentally disordered sentenced prisoners to hospital

correct_answers.text: Section 48 allows transfer of mentally disordered sentenced prisoners to hospital

questions.explanation: Section 47 allows transfer of a mentally disordered sentenced prisoner to hospital and needs reports from two medical practitioners addressing the category of mental disorder and whether it is of a nature and degree to warrant hospital admission.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false?

options.text: Diminished responsibility leads to acquittal of the person
A person is unfit to stand trial when that person is so unwell that appearance at court would be detrimental to his or her health
Fitness to plead is different from fitness to stand trial
The Pritchard criteria are used in assessing fitness to plead in England and Wales
In a case of a mother killing her baby when the infant is under 12 months old, the court may convict her of infanticide rather than murder

correct_answer.text: Diminished responsibility leads to acquittal of the person

correct_answers.text: Diminished responsibility leads to acquittal of the person

questions.explanation: Diminished responsibility may lead to conviction for the lesser offence of manslaughter but does not result in acquittal.

questions.question_text: In what percentage of domestic violence are women the victim?
questions.explanation: 70% of incidents of domestic violence have women as the victim.

questions.question_text: In which of the following age groups are crime rates highest among males?

options.text: 22–26 years
14–17 years
30–35 years
38–42 years
50–55 years

correct_answer.text: 14–17 years

correct_answers.text: 14–17 years

questions.explanation: Males aged 10–20 years account for 50% of crimes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most prevalent crime in England and Wales?

options.text: Sexual offences
Robbery
Theft
Drug offences
Violence against another person

correct_answer.text: Theft

correct_answers.text: Theft

questions.explanation: Theft is the most common crime (about 41% of all crime) in England and Wales.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding malpractice?The plaintiff must establish through the evidence that:

options.text: A doctor–patient relationship existed that created a duty of care
There was a deviation from the standard of care
The patient was damaged
The deviation directly caused the damage
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: The plaintiff (i.e. the patient) or his or her family or estate must establish that there existed a doctor–patient relationship, that there was a deviation of standard care, that the patient was damaged and that the deviation directly caused the damage.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding legal automatism?

options.text: Legal automatism results in increased punishment
Night terrors are a type of automatism
Sane automatism is caused by intrinsic factors
Concussions and dissociative states can lead to insane automatism
It is the same as automatism that occurs in complex partial seizures

correct_answer.text: Night terrors are a type of automatism

correct_answers.text: Night terrors are a type of automatism

questions.explanation: Legal automatisms result in decreased punishment and even acquittal. Sane automatism is due to extrinsic factors, while insane is due to intrinsic factors.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding arson?

options.text: The male:female ratio is 9:1
Only a small proportion of arson offences lead to prosecution
In patients with psychotic illness, arson is frequently an indirect effect of chronic illness rather than a result of delusions or hallucinations
The rate of further arson is 80%
The rate of any reoffence is 10–30%

correct_answer.text: The rate of further arson is 80%

correct_answers.text: The rate of further arson is 80%

questions.explanation: The rate of further acts of arson is 2–20%. Males most commonly commit arson offences.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false regarding exhibitionism?

options.text: It is commonly seen in younger adults
Females are the usual victims
Most exhibitionists have low IQ
It is different from indecent exposure
Flashing and mooning are types of exhibitionism

correct_answer.text: Most exhibitionists have low IQ

correct_answers.text: Most exhibitionists have low IQ

questions.explanation: Most have a normal IQ. Exhibitionism is more commonly seen in young adults than in elderly people.
